Section 0 also holds two rules that read no data at all, only the date: the halving cycle (long from 18 months before a halving, short from 18 months after, covering at 30 months straight back into long -- never in cash) and the US election cycle (long from 23 months before, short from 12 months after, cash from 24 months after until the next 23-month mark). The schedule is the one supplied on 2026-09-21, each change filled the day after its signal, and each rule already holds a position on 2015-01-01 from the cycle before. They short from their own first flip, not from the 2018 date the dashboard rows use; each note gives what that convention would make instead. A cycle rule fitted to cycles that have already happened is the purest form of hindsight: four halvings and three elections are the whole sample

2018-01-01 on the dashboard rows (sections 1-4), as on the dashboard: before it, wherever a book would be short it is flat. Long positions keep their own start. The screen/workbook checks apply the same date to the screen's triggers, so they stay like for like.

Section 2 scores only the SHORT periods of each published signal: short when the dashboard is short, flat otherwise, on fixed coins. Equity above 1.0x = the shorts made money. x B&H and excess are blank because buy and hold is not a short leg's benchmark; time in market = share of days short; trades and hit = short trades and the share that made money. A fixed-coin short marked daily is worth nothing once BTC is up 100% at any point in its hold, and stays at zero.
